chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Al-Qasim al-Sayrafi, the partner of Al-Mufaddal, said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Islam is that by which blood is saved (from being shed), and by which trusts are fulfilled, and by which private parts are made permissible (for intimacy), and the reward is based upon faith.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four main benefits or functions of Islam mentioned in this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the four pillars of Islamic identity: the sanctity of life, the integrity of trusts, the legitimacy of marital relations, and the spiritual merit of faith. In Shia scholarship, this is often viewed as a comprehensive definition of Islam that integrates legal status (fiqh) with spiritual reality (iman), emphasizing that true submission manifests in both social contracts and divine reward.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hakam Bin Ayman, from Al Qasim Al Sayrafi Shareek Al Mufazaal who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Al-Islām, the blood is saved by it, and the entrustments are paid by it, and the private parts are made to be Permissible by it, and the Rewards are based upon the Emān (faith)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ’Umayr from al- Hakam ibn Ayman from al-Qasim al-Sayrafi associate of al-Mufaddal who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Islam is to spare lives, protect the trust and make the marriage lawful, but reward comes from faith and belief.’”
